title: Morning Edition
notes: Morning Edition for Thursday, Nov 5, 2026 — the first regular once-daily update after the publishing pause. It covers developments since Wednesday evening.

The lead is the post-midterm House leadership shake-up. Hong Kong’s Joshua Wong sentencing, Canada’s Budget 2026 day, China’s Ma Xingrui indictment and White House Ukraine–Russia talks round out the top stories.
Hong Kong has five stories; the U.S., Canada, China and World have three each. There is no U.S. culture story this morning; we did not pad one.

Some outlet pages refused automated downloads or only partly loaded (noted under Sources & checks); that is an access limit, not a broken link. The federal budget is still scheduled for this afternoon, so we use planned tense until it is tabled.
provenance: House seat totals still move as ballots are counted. The Guardian interactive (updated early Thursday) showed Democrats at 240 House seats with 387 of 435 races called; CNN’s live blog said the network projects Democrats will win at least 245. We give each figure with its source.

AP article pages and some CBC/Axios pages triggered bot challenges (HTTP 403 / empty body) in this run; we cite NBC, CBS, RTHK, government releases and other pages that did load, and mark the AP/Axios limits.

stories.headline: Johnson steps aside as House GOP leader; Jeffries launches bid to be the first Black Speaker
stories.deck: A day after Democrats took the House, Speaker Mike Johnson told staff he will not seek minority leader. Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan are already running, while Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries asked colleagues for Speakership support.
stories.summary: A day after Democrats took the House, Speaker Mike Johnson told staff he will not seek minority leader. Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan are already running, while Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries asked colleagues for Speakership support. NBC News, citing four people on a Wednesday staff call, said Johnson will not stay on as Republican leader when the new Congress meets. Republicans are scheduled to pick their candidate for minority leader in an internal vote on Nov. 10. Scalise, the No. 2 House Republican, wrote colleagues that “last night’s election was far worse than any of us expected” and announced his bid; Jordan, the Judiciary Committee chair, also entered in a Wednesday letter. Jeffries, in a Nov. 4 dear-colleague letter from his office, formally asked for support to serve as Speaker of the 120th Congress. NBC separately reported that Jeffries faces no opposition in the Democratic caucus and would need a House floor election in January to take the gavel. CBS News said Jeffries expects Democrats to win at least 255 House seats after counting finishes and told reporters no one in the caucus had raised impeaching President Trump.
stories.why: Who leads each party in the House will shape investigations, the legislative calendar and how a Democratic majority deals with a Republican president when the new Congress convenes in January.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Johnson’s decision was reported by NBC from a private staff call; Scalise’s and Jeffries’ letters are on the record. The Speakership is not decided until the House elects a Speaker in January.

stories.headline: Mississippi’s Senate race heads for provisional ballots as dozens of House seats stay uncalled
stories.deck: Two days after the midterms, Alaska and Mississippi still have no Senate race call, and tens of House seats remain open. The open races will set the size of Democratic majorities, not which party leads.
stories.summary: Two days after the midterms, Alaska and Mississippi still have no Senate race call, and tens of House seats remain open. The open races will set the size of Democratic majorities, not which party leads. The Guardian’s results board, updated early Thursday, showed the Senate at 54 Democrats (including two independents) to 44 Republicans with 33 of 35 races called, and the House at 240 Democrats to 147 Republicans with 387 of 435 races called. CNN’s Thursday live blog said the network projects Democrats will win at least 245 House seats, rates Alaska as favoring the Democrat and Mississippi as neutral, and reported Democrat Scott Colom leading Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by just over 1,000 votes with about 96% of ballots in — a race expected to turn on roughly 15,000 provisional (affidavit) ballots that may not be resolved until next week. NPR scheduled a Thursday segment on the remaining House and Senate contests with the Cook Political Report. Race-by-race detail remains in our Midterms 2026 special edition.
stories.why: Every remaining seat changes how much room Democratic leaders have to pass bills, launch investigations and sustain veto overrides when the new Congress meets.
stories.label: Reported
stories.note: Seat totals move as ballots are counted. Donna Daily does not call races; figures are as published by the linked outlets on Thursday morning.

stories.headline: Carney’s second budget is set to be tabled this afternoon, framed as economic resilience
stories.deck: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is scheduled to table Budget 2026 in the Commons on Thursday afternoon. Previews cast it as a plan to harden Canada against U.S. trade shocks and other disruptions.
stories.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is scheduled to table Budget 2026 in the Commons on Thursday afternoon. Previews cast it as a plan to harden Canada against U.S. trade shocks and other disruptions. A Department of Finance media advisory earlier set the Nov. 5 release date and said the budget would outline steps to build a “stronger, more independent and more resilient economy,” unlock investment and advance nation-building projects. CityNews, carrying Canadian Press, said Thursday’s document is Carney’s second budget and will include an update on the federal immigration levels plan; MPs are then expected to debate it for weeks. Champagne has said the budget aims to make Canada more resilient to external shocks such as U.S. trade aggression, Canadian Press reported in a morning roundup. An AFP brief said the plan is designed to reduce reliance on the United States and is expected to fund major projects tagged as crucial to economic sovereignty, including energy and critical-mineral infrastructure.
stories.why: The budget is the government’s main annual statement of spending, borrowing and economic priorities, and it lands two days after a U.S. midterm that reshapes Ottawa’s main trading partner.
stories.label: Official statement + reported
stories.note: As of this Morning Edition the budget had not yet been tabled; wording follows scheduled/preview tense. Details may change when the document is released this afternoon.

stories.headline: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk is set for a second spacewalk to finish the ISS power upgrade
stories.deck: Kutryk and NASA’s Anil Menon are scheduled to leave the station at 8:30 a.m. ET to install the eighth and final roll-out solar array, completing a years-long boost from about 160 to 215 kilowatts.
stories.summary: Kutryk and NASA’s Anil Menon are scheduled to leave the station at 8:30 a.m. ET to install the eighth and final roll-out solar array, completing a years-long boost from about 160 to 215 kilowatts. NASA’s station blog said mission managers gave a go on Wednesday and that the roughly seven-hour excursion mostly repeats the pair’s Oct. 29 tasks on the opposite side of the starboard truss, with Menon riding Canadarm2. CityNews, carrying Canadian Press, said Kutryk became the fifth Canadian to spacewalk on Oct. 29 and that today’s outing is his second in two weeks. Space.com said live coverage was due to begin about an hour before the scheduled start.
stories.why: It is a rare high-profile Canadian role in finishing a multi-year station power upgrade that underpins science and operations on the ISS.

stories.headline: Canadians cheer the blue wave, but many say trust in the U.S. will take more than one election
stories.deck: Street interviews in Toronto found relief at Democratic control of Congress — and little immediate appetite to resume U.S. travel or shopping while tariffs and sovereignty fights linger.
stories.summary: Street interviews in Toronto found relief at Democratic control of Congress — and little immediate appetite to resume U.S. travel or shopping while tariffs and sovereignty fights linger. Canadian Press reported that many Canadians welcome the midterm rebuke of President Trump but doubt it will quickly repair a relationship strained by tariffs, talk of Canada as a 51st state and other provocations. Interviewees described cutting cross-border trips and U.S. products; one said she was “absolutely overjoyed” with the outcome but still not planning a U.S. visit soon. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said Wednesday that Ottawa’s push to diversify trade will not change as Democrats take Congress, and that recent talks with the Trump administration have been productive, CP reported. An opinion essay in The Conversation argued the Democratic sweep could put Canada–U.S. ties on firmer footing and noted the trade war featured in Maine’s Senate race.
stories.why: Public opinion and diversification policy shape how far Ottawa softens its hedge against Washington even after a friendlier Congress.
stories.label: Reported + analysis
stories.note: Street quotes are as reported by Canadian Press. The Conversation piece is marked analysis/opinion in our reading of it.

stories.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years for conspiring to collude with foreign forces
stories.deck: The High Court jailed the activist after a guilty plea under the national security law. Two months and two days will run with his existing subversion sentence; he is not due for release until late 2036 on current terms.
stories.summary: The High Court jailed the activist after a guilty plea under the national security law. Two months and two days will run with his existing subversion sentence; he is not due for release until late 2036 on current terms. Judge William Tam called the offence “grave,” took a 13-year starting point and cut three years for the plea, leaving the 10-year statutory minimum for a grave offence, RTHK reported. A government press release said Wong pleaded guilty on Sept. 2 to conspiring with absconder Nathan Law and others to solicit foreign sanctions or hostile measures against China and Hong Kong. Chief Executive John Lee said Wong and his associates were among the “primary culprits” who undermined prosperity and stability; police national security officers welcomed the sentence. BBC and The Guardian noted Wong, 30, rose to fame in the 2014 Umbrella Movement and had been due for release in January before the new term.
stories.why: It is the second national-security conviction for Hong Kong’s best-known activist and extends his imprisonment well into the next decade under Beijing’s 2020 security law.
stories.label: Official statement + reported
stories.note: Court findings and government statements are presented as such; critics’ view that the security law silences dissent is attributed to BBC/Guardian framing, not adopted as Donna Daily’s finding.

stories.headline: Melania Trump is set to host Ukrainian and Russian officials at the White House as Abu Dhabi talks near
stories.deck: The first lady’s office cast Thursday’s meeting as follow-up to a local ceasefire she helped mediate around occupied Oleshky. Broader U.S.–Ukraine–Russia talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11.
stories.summary: The first lady’s office cast Thursday’s meeting as follow-up to a local ceasefire she helped mediate around occupied Oleshky. Broader U.S.–Ukraine–Russia talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11. The Independent reported that Melania Trump would personally convene representatives from both sides and deliver remarks on the nearly six-day local halt in fighting. RTE said President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described a detailed 90-minute call with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and that negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States are due in Abu Dhabi for the first three-way talks since February. stories.headline: Herzog’s coalition consultations enter a decisive day as Eisenkot leads recommendations
stories.deck: Israel’s president began meeting party leaders after accepting certified election results. Early tallies of recommendations put Gadi Eisenkot ahead of Benjamin Netanyahu, with no candidate yet assured of 61 seats.
stories.summary: Israel’s president began meeting party leaders after accepting certified election results. Early tallies of recommendations put Gadi Eisenkot ahead of Benjamin Netanyahu, with no candidate yet assured of 61 seats. Al Jazeera, with AP, said Herzog’s acceptance of the results on Wednesday undercut Netanyahu’s efforts to cast the Oct. 27 vote as illegitimate after his bloc lost its majority. The Jerusalem Post reported Thursday’s second-round consultations, including Ra’am recommending Eisenkot. Liveblog tallies circulating Thursday put Eisenkot near 56 recommendations to Netanyahu’s mid-40s, with United Torah Judaism declining to endorse anyone — figures that can still shift before Herzog assigns an exploratory mandate.
stories.why: Herzog’s choice of whom to task with forming a government will set whether Israel gets a Netanyahu comeback attempt or an Eisenkot-led alternative coalition.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine trade overnight drone strikes on logistics and energy sites
stories.deck: Moscow said it hit a Nova Poshta hub, a power substation and a cargo ship; Ukrainian drones sparked fires around Ryazan’s industrial zone, a regional governor said.
stories.summary: Moscow said it hit a Nova Poshta hub, a power substation and a cargo ship; Ukrainian drones sparked fires around Ryazan’s industrial zone, a regional governor said. Al Jazeera reported Russia’s defence ministry claimed drone hits on a Nova Poshta terminal near Kharkiv, a 330-kV substation in Dnipropetrovsk region and a dry-cargo ship southwest of Odesa. Ryazan’s governor said more than 200 Ukrainian drones struck overnight, with debris fires and brief power cuts and one person injured. Kharkiv’s governor reported more than 80 drones across the region over a day, injuring six people including a child. The Independent’s live blog separately noted continuing fallout from Monday’s school strike in Zaporizhzhia that Ukraine says killed 40 people.
stories.why: The cross-border infrastructure strikes keep pressure on both sides even as White House and Abu Dhabi diplomacy accelerates.
